note: Live-session recording of the screen scenes (series/tools/rec). prepare/teardown run on the laptop, not recorded; commands are typed and run for real. Servers are started hidden by prepare (helper %TEMP%\mgnet\svc.ps1) and their logs are shown with Get-Content/Select-String. No servers here. The SQL screen needs the owner to type the test login's password (Read-Host) and never prints the connection string. If a test fails on SQL Server, report the error; do not re-record with the tests disabled.

screens.name: test-explorer
steps: Open the episode folder in VS Code (C# Dev Kit); the dotnet build in prepare makes the tests appear
Open the Testing view (beaker icon); expand ProjectRequests.Tests.NUnit and ProjectRequests.Tests.Xunit one or two levels
Click Run Tests at the top: green ticks, two skipped (the SQL Server tests)
In the integrated terminal (pwsh) run: ./deploy/Invoke-Tests.ps1  -> 'Test run summary: Passed!', total: 69, succeeded: 67, skipped: 2

screens.name: coverage-report
steps: Open the page prepared by ./deploy/Invoke-Tests.ps1 -Mode Coverage (local file, nothing to sign in to)
Show 'Parser: MultiReport (2x Cobertura)', line coverage about 93 %, branch coverage about 89 %
Scroll to the class list: PriorityRules at 50 %
Click PriorityRules: the two const decimal lines in red, both methods green

screens.name: sqlserver-lab
prepare: if (-not (Test-NetConnection 10.50.0.30 -Port 1433 -WarningAction SilentlyContinue).TcpTestSucceeded) { throw 'CON-SQL01 (10.50.0.30:1433) is not reachable: start the lab with Start-MGLab.ps1' }

$has = Invoke-Command -VMName CON-SQL01 -Credential $cred { sqlcmd -S localhost -E -h -1 -W -Q "SET NOCOUNT ON; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sys.server_principals WHERE name = 'requests_tests'" }; if ("$has".Trim() -ne '1') { throw 'SQL login requests_tests is missing on CON-SQL01: create it first (demo.md, dbcreator role, password typed by the recorder)' }

$sec = Read-Host 'Password of the SQL login requests_tests (typed by the recorder, never stored)' -AsSecureString; $b = [System.Data.Common.DbConnectionStringBuilder]::new(); $b['Server'] = '10.50.0.30'; $b['User ID'] = 'requests_tests'; $b['Password'] = (ConvertFrom-SecureString $sec -AsPlainText); $b['TrustServerCertificate'] = 'True'; $env:REQUESTS_TEST_SQLSERVER = $b.ConnectionString
mask: the connection string must never be printed (the commands never echo it)

teardown: Invoke-Command -VMName CON-SQL01 -Credential $cred { sqlcmd -S localhost -E -Q "SELECT name FROM sys.databases WHERE name LIKE 'ProjectRequests[_]%'; IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM sys.server_principals WHERE name = 'requests_tests') DROP LOGIN requests_tests" }
needs: sql-login:requests_tests (created by the owner on CON-SQL01, password typed at recording time)
